---
title: 'CI reconciler'
description: 'Observe declared current-head CI gates and retain bounded recovery evidence.'
---

## Initial rollout: dry-run

The CI reconciler initially observes only. The checked-in policy at
`scripts/ci/ci-reconciler-policy.json` disables recovery. Missing or invalid policy
fails closed; a workflow input cannot enable recovery. Mutation activation requires
an exact-source Security ACK and the release owner's freeze lift after dry-run
acceptance. Source review alone does not establish scheduled or hosted execution.

The workflow `.github/workflows/ci-reconciler.yaml` runs on standard
`ubuntu-latest` runners, with no dependency installation or application build.
It uses GitHub's built-in job token; no provider credential is required. The
fifteen-minute schedule is a desired observation cadence, not a recovery SLA.
Hosted queue delays and schedule coalescing can delay execution.

## Coverage and identity

The trusted operational manifest explicitly names eight core producers:

- Test
- TypeScript Type Check
- Oxc Check
- i18n Check
- Security Checks
- CodeQL Manual Fallback
- Codex Plugin Check
- Required account MFA database contract

CodeQL runs on pushes only for security-sensitive paths, so a head without a
CodeQL run is expected; the nightly Security Checks schedule scans it.

The manifest covers `main` and `production` explicitly. It is not proof that all
apps, builds, Mobile checks, or release requirements are green. App applicability
and Mobile qualification remain with their owning release/check owners. New
branches and gates require reviewed policy entries; historical release branches
are not discovered and activated automatically.

The controller reads the operational manifest and Actions history. Comparison
with effective required-check rules is separate proposed work. Missing GitHub
required-check configuration is a known enforcement gap, not proof of zero
required coverage. External/manual gates remain outside this manifest; they are
never replaced with synthetic success.

Each Actions summary identifies the branch head and declared gate count:

```text
HEAD <sha>: <N> required, all terminal
HEAD <sha>: <N> required, <M> missing
```

Failed terminal checks appear separately. **All terminal does not mean all
green.** Deterministic failures stay failed and return to their source owner.
Cancelled and missing checks are recovery candidates; queued or running matches
are deduplicated.

## Trust and recovery boundaries

Only `tutur3u/platform` on the trusted `main` workflow ref can plan. Only the
`schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` events are accepted. The workflow declares no
`workflow_run` trigger because the producers it observes also run in merge
groups, and the workflow policy forbids a completion consumer chained from a
merge group run. Both jobs check out
`github.workflow_sha`, never upstream branch code or artifact code.

Planning has `actions: read` and `contents: read`. Recovery alone has
`actions: write` and `contents: read`. Jobs have five-minute timeouts and the
workflow serializes runs without cancellation. The recovery matrix contains only
branches with actual admitted actions and executes one branch at a time.

When recovery is enabled through reviewed source policy, the controller re-reads
HEAD immediately before every mutation and stops an old plan if HEAD advances.
It may rerun a cancelled allowlisted run at the exact current SHA or dispatch a
supported allowlisted workflow after exact-head admission. It never cancels
protected runs or retries deterministic failures into green. Dispatch identity
requires API readback; an ambiguous write outcome requires reconciliation rather
than blind replay.

`Test` declares no `workflow_dispatch` trigger, so the manifest marks it as
rerun-only; a missing `Test` run is reported, never dispatched.

Recovery is capped at three attempts per branch/head/workflow/policy identity,
with one-, five- and fifteen-minute backoff across subsequent ticks. No sleeping
worker holds a runner. Bounded API history and pagination must be complete enough
to establish eligibility; unavailable or truncated history blocks recovery.

This workflow never starts releases, deployments, staging/production migrations,
or provider publication. The disposable account-MFA CI contract is not a
production migration. It does not write branch rulesets or provider settings.

## Durable receipts

Planning uploads an intent **before** the recovery job can start:

| Artifact | Retention | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ci-reconcile-intent-<branch>-<sha>` | 30 days | Durable operation intent and dedupe identity |
| `ci-reconcile-result-<branch>-<sha>` | 30 days | Recovery outcome and readback |
| `ci-reconcile-observe-<run_id>-<run_attempt>` | 7 days | Read-only observation report |

The recovery job downloads only the exact branch/SHA intent from its own workflow
run. Artifact content is data for the trusted controller, never executable code.
An observation artifact does not count as a recovery intent or attempt.

The recovery head-age fence is 20 days, inside the 30-day receipt retention
window. Recovery fails closed before an expired ledger could make an old attempt
look new. Missing, expired, unavailable or incomplete durable history is a block,
not an empty retry budget. Preserve receipts when investigating unknown outcomes.

## Acceptance and stop procedure

Before enabling recovery, require focused controller and workflow tests for
head races, dedupe, concurrent events, retry caps and backoff, unknown outcomes,
unsupported workflows, invalid policy, external contexts, recursive triggers and
release/migration exclusions. Require exact-source independent Security review,
then dry-run scheduled receipts. Verify that failed
checks remain visible and that no mutation occurs with recovery disabled.

Stop recovery by disabling it in trusted source policy. Stop observation through
the repository's authorized workflow control if needed. Neither action grants
permission to change release gates. After any source change, repeat the relevant
exact-source review and hosted acceptance; old receipts do not prove a new head.

A separate proposal can enforce the validated manifest through a public-repository
GitHub Free ruleset. It needs a dry-run comparison of conditional checks and App
identities and its own exact Security ACK before any ruleset write. This proposal
is outside the initial rollout and is not performed by the reconciler.

See the [GitHub Actions runbook](/build/devops/github-actions-runbook) for the
remaining validation and delivery evidence requirements.
